The player who played the highest card takes a positive point card and the player with the lowest card gets stuck with a negative point card as you try to get the highest score., INCLUDES: 75 Player Cards, 15 Point Cards, Illustrated Instructions, EASY TO LEARN: Brief how-to-play video available online; Description: To win this game, you'll need to read your opponent's minds - when you figure out which card they're about to play you'll have your chance to win. On each turn, players flip over a point card and compete to take it (if it's a positive number) or avoid it (if it's a negative number). history.text: I want a card game.
What's your budget? For example $15-30, under $15 or $60-120.
My budget is up to $50.
What kind exactly are you looking for — collectible card games, decks and sets or dedicated deck card games?
A card game.
How old is the child?
My kid is 14 years old.

Here are card games that fit a 14-year-old and a budget of up to $50.
1. Poop: The Game - Public Restroom Edition (Price: $10.00; Average rating: 4.2/5 (163 reviews); Store: Breaking Games)
   A family-friendly card game with a manufacturer recommended age of 14 years and up, priced at $10, well within the $50 budget. [E1]
2. AMIGO What The Heck? Strategy Card Game (Price: $10.90; Average rating: 4.6/5 (44 reviews); Store: AMIGO)
   A strategy card game for ages 8+ and 2-5 players, priced at $10.90, comfortably under the $50 budget. [E3]
3. Play-2-Learn Go Fish: Hooked on Friendship Game (Price: $19.95; Average rating: 5.0/5 (3 reviews); Store: Franklin Learning Systems)
   A card game priced at $19.95, within the $50 budget, though its stated grade levels (K-2, 3-5) suggest it is aimed at younger children rather than a 14-year-old. [E4]
